extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing to publish in Selecta Mathematica (mathematicians considering submission)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on publishing options (subscription vs open access), article processing charges, funding routes, and Creative Commons licence choices when publishing in the journal Selecta Mathematica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing options (hybrid journal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecta Mathematica is a hybrid journal; once the article is accepted authors may choose between subscription publishing or open access publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both options will be offered after acceptance. Choosing a route affects licensing, access, and potential APCs. Authors should select the route that meets any funder or institutional mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription publishing model
rubrics_metrics.description: Published articles are made available to institutions and individuals who subscribe to the journal or who pay to read specific articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you select the subscription route you accept the journal’s standard licensing terms. This route is unsuitable if your funder requires immediate open access (e.g., NIH or Plan S). Subscription authors must warrant they have not already committed to terms inconsistent with the journal's licensing agreement, including any embargo period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access publishing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access publication requires the author(s) or funder(s) to pay an article processing charge (APC); the final published version is then free to read for everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access should be selected when funders or institutions require immediate accessibility on publication (for example NIH or Plan S members). The publisher will assist authors in choosing the correct route to comply with mandates. Authors may need to take specific actions to achieve compliance with funder/institutional OA mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: APC charging timing and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The APC price is determined from the date on which the article is accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The APC applicable is set by the acceptance date; plan funding accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current APC amount and taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Current APC for Selecta Mathematica: £2390.00 GBP / $3290.00 USD / €2690.00 EUR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fee is subject to VAT or local taxes where applicable. Check the journal's open access support portal and Journal pricing FAQs for further information and any updates to pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to avoid or cover APCs (funding routes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may save on APCs via institutional agreements or by accessing open access funding from research funders and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature offers agreements enabling institutions to cover OA publishing costs; authors should check institutional eligibility and whether the journal is included. Authors can also consult Springer Nature’s open access funding and support services for further options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons licence options for OA articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access articles in Selecta Mathematica are published under either CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International or CC BY 4.0 International licences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC BY-NC-ND: article may be shared for non-commercial purposes with author credit; permission required for commercial reuse or adapted/derivative versions. CC BY: article may be shared and adapted for any purpose (including commercial) provided authors are credited. Authors retain copyright of their articles under these licences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence selection and funder/institution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may need licence variations to meet funder or institutional open access licence requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the publisher’s guide to licensing, copyright and author rights for journal articles to choose licence variations that satisfy specific funder or institutional mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of publishing open access
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access publishing offers increased reach and readership: reported higher citations, downloads, and Altmetric attention compared with non-OA articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature cites aggregated metrics: OA articles 1.6x more citations, 4x more downloads, and 2.5x more Altmetric attention (including 1.9x more news mentions and 1.2x more policy mentions). Use these considerations when deciding between OA and subscription.
